_what: The one settings file for the kit's tools. Change the values for your project; the tools read it. It is a protected file: a build session cannot change it (tools/hooks/protect_tests.py).

slos._what: The targets the weekly scorecard judges against. A missed target is an error budget spent: reliability work comes before new work (faults first).

spend._what: The month's spend is the larger of the ledger (every paid run, estimate before, actual after) and the bills copied from each provider. tools/spend.py reads both. The hard backstop is the cap the owner sets on each provider's own billing page.

auto_merge._what: The green lane: the AI merges its own pull request only when tools/checks/lane.py --pr <n> says MERGE OK.

red_lane._what: Paths that put a pull request in the red lane: the AI never merges it; it waits for the owner (NEXT.md, 'Waiting on owner'). ** = any folders. Also red: an existing test changed or deleted, the test floor lowered, a new app (or a changed plan or cap) in docs/APPS.yaml. Raising the test floor is green.

roles._what: Which model does each job. Chosen by current independent rankings (for example LMArena, Artificial Analysis, SWE-bench), mixing vendors freely. The reviewer is a different model, and a different vendor where possible, from the builder. Every value below is a DEFAULT TO REVISIT, picked 18 Nov 2026 from the vendors' own release notes, not from a ranking: the weekly review checks the rankings and changes them. claude_code is the alias the .claude/agents files use when the role runs inside Claude Code.

coordinator.job: plans, hands out steps, merges through the green-lane gate, writes the morning summary

builder.job: writes the code for one work order, test first

reviewer.job: reads the finished diff it did not write and passes or fails it (prompts/reviewer-brief.md); run in Codex or another tool of the other vendor, Claude Code only as the fallback

reader.job: reads many saved pages and writes one structured result per item

scout.job: read-only look-ups: inventories, terms pages, large files
